issue_context.title: supporting t5 for question answering
issue_context.body:
# 🚀 Feature request

Hi, this would be great and appreciated to support t5 model for run_qa.py script, currently this does not support it.

## Motivation

T5 is the state of the art model, for which there are a lot of motivation for people in NLP community to use this model, specially it can handle multiple datasets.


## Your contribution

<!-- Is there any way that you could help, e.g. by submitting a PR?
     Make sure to read the CONTRIBUTING.MD readme:
     https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->
comments:
Hey @dorooddorood606, 

Since T5 is essentially a text-to-text model, the question-answering task can simply be framed as a seq2seq task. 

I think we could add a `run_qa_seq2seq.py` to https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/master/examples/pytorch/question-answering that is very similar to https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/master/examples/pytorch/summarization/run_summarization.py (we would just need to adapt the dataset to choose from I think). Would you be interested in adding such an example? 

Also pinging @sgugger here to hear his opinion :-)
We could definitely add this kind of example. We just need a proper dataset, as you mentioned.

Dear @sgugger @patrickvonplaten 
Thank you very much for considering my request.

In T5 codebase, for superglue-record, they convert each example to multiple ones for each answer choice [1]. During evaluation though they consider all answer choices. I assume this is the case with most of the QA datasets. In T5 script, since we need seq2seq format, I am not sure how I can handle keeping a set of answers.

thank you very much for your comment in advance.

[1] https://github.com/google-research/text-to-text-transfer-transformer/blob/3c58859b8fe72c2dbca6a43bc775aa510ba7e706/t5/data/preprocessors.py#L918
Cool! @dorooddorood606 would you like to give it a try to make a `run_qa_seq2seq.py` example for SUPERGLUE? Happy to guide you through it :-)

review_comments: Do we have other datasets we could put here? Squad is extractive question answering, so a better example would use a dataset where the answers are not exactly in the context.

@sgugger I couldn't find any dataset where the answer doesn't belong to a context or any other property.

The `t5` repository uses `TriviaQA`, `SQuAD`, and `ReCoRD` datasets which are all extractive datasets having a passage/context for a given query/question. They use the format `context: <context> question: <question>` for input and output as the `answer` to train the model.
ROUGE is a metric used for summarization, not for question-answering, so will this fail?
No, this is the metric used in the script here.
Hmm ok. Aren't QA models tested on F1/exact match? ROUGE is just n-gram overlap

@NielsRogge I couldn't use squad metric as it requires `id` as well which is not being kept track when using a `Seq2Seq` model. Hence I had to use `ROUGE` metric and this doesn't fail the tests.

I can fix this choice of metric in a follow up PR, do you have any suggestion for the metric ?
Extractive QA models yes, I'm not familiar with how generative QA models are usually evaluated.

Doesn't a metric depend on the task, rather than the model? 

e.g. SQuAD is evaluated on F1/exact match
e.g. DROP is evaluated on F1/exact match

How a model comes up with an answer doesn't matter (extractive/generative), we just care about whether it comes up with the correct answers. The T5 authors seem to have used F1 and exact match to evaluate their model on SQuAD (see [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683)).
Feel free to make a PR to fix this :-)

@karthikrangasai would be great if you have the time to update this in a future PR :) it would require writing a `postprocess_qa_predictions` method, similar to the one used in the `run_qa.py` script. It would be very similar, however instead of turning `start_logits` and `end_logits` into actual predicted answers (which is what extractive models do), it would be a bit simpler as the model just generates an answer.

Let me know if you need any help!
@sgugger @NielsRogge Sure, I will create a new PR for this.
